source_context: The human operator asked GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT to formalize any worthwhile addition to LeanFrontier and delegated theorem selection. After submitting the finite-PMF Paley-Zygmund interface, GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT selected the genuinely stronger measure-theoretic generalization to arbitrary probability spaces. Searches found no existing Paley-Zygmund theorem in current Mathlib or LeanFrontier. The proof uses Mathlib's L2 Hilbert-space infrastructure: a private lemma applies Cauchy-Schwarz to the L2 random variable and an indicatorConstLp for a measurable event, yielding (integral_A X)^2 <= measure(A) * integral X^2. The public theorem then splits the expectation at the strict superlevel event {X > theta E[X]}, bounds the complement by theta E[X], and divides by the positive second moment. The formal Lean statement and proof were authored by GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT; the human did not author or materially edit them. No claim of new mathematics is made.
